cases.title: Hermite-smoothed initial states
cases.semanticTier: General-order Hermite samples and an explicit real-rotation preparation
cases.problem: Prepare the sampled smooth auxiliary initial state used in Schrödingerisation, for any Hermite order k. Load function values as amplitudes and account for the preparation circuit itself.
cases.contract: The exact target uses exp(p) to the left of −1, a degree-at-most 2k+1 Hermite polynomial on [−1,0], and exp(−p) to the right of 0. The real-valued samples are normalized before preparation. The circuit uses explicit uniformly controlled real rotations, compiled to Ry and CNOT. The exact symbolic theorem and finite floating-point export checks have separate scopes.
symbols: Number of endpoint derivatives matched; k=1 is the cubic splice.
Qubit count and sample count. q0 has weight 1.
Real amplitude before normalization, not a measurement probability.
Sum of squared samples; normalization is proved from the actual input.

circuit.registers: q0 is the least significant bit. Layers prepare q0, q1, …, q(n−1). No ancilla or output measurement. Kets print q(n−1)…q0.

stages.label: Classical sample construction
stages.detail: Compute the Hermite coefficients and evaluate the two tails and the polynomial splice.

stages.label: Mass reduction
stages.detail: Sum squared amplitudes over common low-bit prefixes. Each parent mass is the sum of its children.

stages.label: Quantum preparation
stages.detail: Apply one uniformly controlled Ry layer per qubit, then compile every layer to Ry and CNOT.

stages.label: Prepared register
stages.detail: The final amplitudes equal the normalized samples. Independent finite replay measures numerical rounding error.

evolution.caption: A single reference construction connects the Hermite sample theorem to its Ry/CNOT preparation. The displayed n=3 costs describe the illustrative serial sequence. This is a construction and proof trace; no optimization history or comparative resource improvement is claimed.

stages.name: Hermite rotation tree
stages.instructionTier: Illustrative n=3 reference sequence: 7 Ry and 8 CX; depth 15 is the serial schedule, not an optimized depth claim.
stages.description: First construct the polynomial and its endpoint jets. Build the low-bit mass tree and apply its exact controlled rotations. The invariant says that a prefix carries the square root of its total remaining probability mass. The final layer resolves each requested amplitude.

qiskit.role: Replays the actual Ry/CNOT gate list using independent NumPy and Qiskit evaluators and an OpenQASM round trip. Reports finite floating-point evidence, not a general exact certificate.

cases.summary: Turn a smooth function into a concrete quantum state: explicit Hermite coefficients, a mass-tree proof, elementary rotation gates, and reproducible finite exports.
cases.limitations: Ideal real-angle gates are the symbolic model. Floating-point sampling and exported angles are checked numerically on reported finite instances. PDE recovery, Sobolev regularity, Fourier convergence, hardware angle synthesis, and global circuit optimality are outside this state-preparation certificate.

hermite-smooth-state-preparation.readerGoal: A smooth classical curve becomes the amplitudes of a quantum register.
hermite-smooth-state-preparation.whyThisCase: Smoothing the auxiliary initial condition removes a derivative jump. A quantum algorithm still needs a circuit that loads the resulting samples. This case shows every step between the function and its state-preparation gates.
hermite-smooth-state-preparation.algorithmContext: In Schrödingerisation, this register is prepared independently of the physical-system initial state. Their joint input is |g_k> tensor |u_0>. Subsequent Fourier transforms and evolution are separate algorithm stages.

source.title: Schrödingerisation based computationally stable algorithms for ill-posed problems in partial differential equations
source.authors: Shi Jin, Nana Liu and Chuwen Ma
source.queryExplanation: Section 4.3, Eqs. (4.31)–(4.32), fixes the smooth initial-data family. ASPBE supplies the state-preparation construction; this page does not claim to formalize the PDE convergence estimate.

circuitReading: q0 is the low bit. Label j is the sum of 2^r q_r; the rightmost bit in a ket is q0.
At layer d, the already prepared low bits choose an angle on qubit qd. Higher bits are still zero.
A rotation sends the square root of a parent mass into square roots of its two child masses.
Half-sum and half-difference rotation tables plus CNOT pairs realize the same selected two-dimensional rotation.
The concrete gate diagram and QASM show finite rounded angles. The symbolic theorem concerns exact real angles.

theorems.label: 1 · Source construction
theorems.title: One polynomial satisfies all endpoint derivative conditions
theorems.statementProse: The coefficients are explicit. At the left endpoint all derivatives through order k equal exp(−1); at the right they alternate between 1 and −1. The polynomial degree is at most 2k+1. The literal piecewise function is globally Cᵏ; a separate gluing theorem closes this analytic claim.
proofSteps: Truncate a formal series
A_k keeps the first k+1 coefficients of exp(t)/(1−t)^(k+1). Multiplication restores the exponential coefficients through order k.
Match each endpoint
A factor t^(k+1) kills the first k derivatives at t=0. Reflect t to 1−t to obtain the right endpoint.
Check uniqueness
A difference with both zero jets is divisible by t^(k+1)(1−t)^(k+1), whose degree is too large unless the difference is zero.
Glue the smooth pieces
Matching values and successive derivatives at −1 and 0 gives a globally Cᵏ real function; Lean proves the gluing for arbitrary k.

theorems.label: 2 · Preparation invariant
theorems.title: The rotations distribute exactly the requested amplitude mass
theorems.statementProse: Every layer resolves one bit of the target state. The squared norm is preserved, and after n layers each leaf amplitude equals its sample divided by the total norm.
proofSteps: Partition by the next bit
The two child index sets are disjoint and together exhaust the parent.
Apply a two-dimensional rotation
Cosine and sine give the ratios of child square-root masses to the parent square-root mass.
Close the root
At full depth each mass is a single squared sample; normalization and state action follow. Zero-mass subtrees carry zero incoming amplitude.

theorems.label: 3 · Read the evidence at the correct level
theorems.title: Exact real-angle gates and finite exported circuits answer different questions
theorems.statementProse: The first identity is the symbolic acceptance target. The second is a measured error for a specified exported instance; the acceptance report supplies the parameters, backend versions and tolerances. The measured tolerance here is the maximum componentwise amplitude error, not a whole-vector Euclidean error.
proofSteps: Keep the real-angle semantics
The generic controlled-rotation compiler preserves the mathematical gate matrix.
Replay the emitted instructions
NumPy, Qiskit and QASM import all consume the actual elementary-gate list rather than a dense preparation black box.
Respect the boundary
A small measured error supports that finite export. It neither proves a uniform floating-point bound nor a PDE convergence theorem.

benchmarkBridge.title: Cubic smoothness: C1, not C2
benchmarkBridge.body: For k=1, P''(0)=−10+8/e whereas the right-hand exponential has second derivative 1. The C2 sentence after source Eq. (6.1) is therefore not adopted. This does not change the endpoint conditions or the preparation target.
